fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents accurately foreground production NLP, Azure, MLflow, serving and drift monitoring without inventing RAG, assistant, CI/CD or pipeline experience. More than five years of overall NLP/ML experience is supported, but four years of specifically documented production ML engineering is not established: the explicit ML engineer role began in March 2023, approximately three years and eight months before this evaluation. The application shows credible adjacent AI-product experience but not chat assistants or RAG, and leaves data versioning, ingestion pipelines, testing and cost optimisation unaddressed.

issues: The relevant NLP publication was omitted.
Python is listed and connected to an early research role, but its use in the current production engineering work could be made more explicit without adding unsupported detail.
The CV is largely a faithful translation rather than a strongly prioritised tailoring for customer-support AI.

reasons: Single-column text extracts in sensible order, with intact names, dates, tools and metrics.
Strong matches for Python, Azure, MLflow, production serving, monitoring and transformer fine-tuning.
Text-dataset preparation and version control are represented semantically through corpus construction and Git, although the exact phrases are absent.
TF-IDF supports a truthful feature-engineering keyword, but the CV does not use that term.
RAG, chat assistants, CI/CD, automated testing and ingestion/training pipelines are absent.
The headline experience duration may satisfy a broad experience filter, but a strict four-year production-ML requirement is not clearly evidenced.

issues: Company specificity is largely limited to the advertised merchant-support mission; it does not draw on Quillstone's ownership, team-first or learning culture.
Much of the letter repeats the CV's technical history rather than developing a sharper argument about transferring complaint classification to support routing.
It does not explicitly distinguish adjacent document-NLP experience from direct assistant or RAG experience, although it also does not claim the latter.
strengths: Names the correct company and exact role.
Uses the supported 94% accuracy and 23-class result.
Connects production serving, monitoring and MLOps to the team's operational responsibilities.
Uses customer-complaint classification as relevant transferable experience.
Maintains an appropriate professional tone and clearly marks doctoral studies as ongoing.

spacing_issues: The CV is fairly dense around the experience section, with little separation between the end of one role and the next role heading.
The cover letter leaves substantial blank space below the signature, consistent with the measured 58.2% fill; this is not excessive for a one-page letter.
consistency_issues: The current job's dates are right-aligned on the heading line, whereas the two earlier roles' dates appear on separate left-aligned lines.
issues: The cover letter lacks a matching contact/name header, so it looks less like a coordinated application set, although the serif typography is consistent.

fluency_and_tone_issues: The letter repeats similar phrases: 'help merchants get support quickly', 'help support teams handle questions and tickets effectively', and 'helping support teams handle merchant inquiries'. These could be condensed.
'build machine learning solutions for practical needs' is vague compared with the otherwise concrete technical evidence.

evaluation.summary: Both documents are accurate, professionally written and readable, with strong evidence for production NLP, Azure deployment, MLflow and monitoring. They preserve the candidate's qualifications and results without inventing RAG experience, certifications or relocation commitments. The main limitations are modest tailoring, omission of the relevant publication, and incomplete evidence for the job's four-year production-ML threshold and several engineering requirements. The clean one-page layouts work well, with only minor density and date-alignment issues.
